circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has been the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The facility represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit to be constructed, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a Melbourne street track encircling Albert Park Lake, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with supporting motorsport events. The venue maintains FIA Grade 1 circuit status and serves as a key fixture on the international racing calendar.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and staged the Austrian Grand Prix continuously between 1970 and 1987. After undergoing modifications and rebranding as the A1-Ring, it returned to hosting the grand prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, situated along Baku Boulevard, and at 6. 003 km represents the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted F1 competition in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before being renamed the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East that year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other motorsport series. The FIA Grade 1 licensed facility supports multiple circuit configurations and has previously accommodated various racing categories including endurance competitions and international touring cars.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design featuring extended straights combined with diverse corner configurations, making it versatile for testing different racing strategies. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian circuit in Wallonia stretches 7. 004 kilometers and ranks among Formula One's most historic venues, having hosted its inaugural Grand Prix in 1925 and the championship's second-ever race in 1950. Since 1985, the track has maintained an unbroken presence on the F1 calendar, aside from gaps in 2003 and 2006, where it continues to stage the Belgian Grand Prix today.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361 km temporary street circuit serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international motorsport series including sports car championships and North American racing categories.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Shanghai's Jiading District, is renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix since 2024, diversifying its major racing events.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated near Northamptonshire that has served as the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948. The circuit gained historic significance by hosting the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, though the British Grand Prix alternated between multiple tracks for several decades before permanently establishing itself at Silverstone from 1987 onwards. Beyond Formula One, the facility also stages MotoGP competition.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the historic 1986 Hungarian Grand Prix, marking the first Formula One race held in an Eastern Bloc nation. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after government officials rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park, and the inaugural race commemorated János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, this 5. 793 km circuit was constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The Italian Grand Prix, held continuously since 1949 except for a 1980 closure during renovations, represents the track's signature event, while its nickname derives from the prolonged straights and swift corners that characterize the layout.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting major international racing events with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is particularly renowned for staging Formula One and Super Formula championship races.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that snakes through Paradise, Nevada, utilizing roads adjacent to the famous Las Vegas Strip along Las Vegas Boulevard. The track passes some of the city's most iconic venues and landmarks, including major hotels and casinos such as Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as well as the MSG Sphere.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two deceased Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in separate racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix intermittently, including a continuous run since 2015 under its current name, the Mexico City Grand Prix.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street course constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One racing, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 as the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street circuit winding through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, circling the harbor of the principality. The track is typically known as Monte Carlo despite being situated across multiple neighborhoods, as most of the route runs through the Monte Carlo area itself.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: The 4. 259 km Dutch racing circuit is situated in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam and resumed hosting Formula One racing in 2021 with the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix, a partnership scheduled to conclude in 2026. Located just 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam and close to the North Sea, the track has operated under various names throughout its history.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is situated near Lusail in northern Qatar, featuring a 5. 419 km layout with a 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aviation accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural year in 2021. The track also began accommodating international electric racing competition from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through downtown Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its road course layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of straightaways and varied corner configurations that test diverse driving skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major motorsport events including MotoGP and endurance racing. The venue has established itself as a premier racing destination, having previously accommodated various international and domestic racing series ranging from IndyCar to sports car competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai national flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 along with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both the Formula One and World Endurance Championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes in Formula One starting in 2025 and has secured six Grand Prix victories since entering the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently driving for Haas in Formula One.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabriel Bortoleto is a Brazilian motorsport competitor who currently races for Audi in Formula One competition.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his 13 seasons in the sport. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, and has secured ten Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto represents Argentina in Formula One, currently racing for Alpine. The driver has established himself on the sport's premier single-seater grid.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines his endurance racing commitments in the European Le Mans Series LMP2 category with a reserve role at Haas, having made multiple Formula One starts during the 2024-2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. He achieved a Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020 while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver of French and Algerian nationality, races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, where he stands as one of the sport's most decorated competitors. He shares the record for seven world championship titles with Michael Schumacher and leads in multiple statistical categories including race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing extensive racing experience to the grid. Beyond his single-seater career, Hülkenberg achieved success in endurance racing by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently racing for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine-season career. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022, demonstrating his status as one of the sport's leading competitors.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen has transitioned from his Formula One career, which spanned 2014-2020 and 2022-2024, to compete primarily in the FIA World Endurance Championship with BMW through the WRT team. He also maintains a part-time racing presence in NASCAR's Cup Series, piloting a Chevrolet for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren, adding to his tally of 12 race victories accumulated over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French motorsport competitor currently driving for Haas in Formula One. Previously racing for Alpine, he achieved a notable victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-season career in the sport. He finished as runner-up in the 2023 drivers' championship while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the sport four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, accumulating eight Grand Prix victories throughout his 14-season career. Known by his nickname "the Honey Badger", Ricciardo established himself as a consistent race winner during his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell represents Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories over the course of eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories during his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American motorsport competitor who raced in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. He has since transitioned to endurance racing, currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following prior involvement in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin. He competes at the highest level of international motorsport under his more commonly used professional name.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese motorsport competitor, has held reserve driver positions with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls throughout his Formula One involvement spanning 2021 to 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has dominated modern Formula One by claiming four consecutive world championships from 2021 to 2024 while accumulating 71 Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, drove in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac, where he continues his involvement in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing operates as Renault's Formula One works team from its Enstone base, competing under the Alpine brand since 2021 before Renault's planned exit at the end of 2025. The squad powered by Mercedes engines has claimed one victory in its Alpine identity, courtesy of Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One across multiple eras through different organizational structures, currently competing under the AMR GP Limited banner as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker and stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad, nicknamed after its emblematic horse symbol, has maintained continuous presence throughout the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas and launched in 2016, the outfit operates under American registration despite being based in Europe. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024 after leading the team since its establishment, Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal position.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, initially built sports cars before shifting to Formula One machinery as an independent manufacturer starting in 1993. Prior to its F1 entry, the operation secured significant endurance racing accolades, including a Le Mans victory in 1989 partnered with Mercedes-Benz. Having operated through numerous iterations across three decades, the constructor ceased competition in 2025 as motorsport's fourth-longest-serving F1 team by race count before being absorbed by Audi.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One team headquartered at its technology facility in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship agreements. The operation functions as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group and is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: The Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, has represented Mercedes-Benz in Formula One since 1954 across various ownership periods. From January 2022, the squad has been jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in equal shares. The team is colloquially known as the "Silver Arrows," a traditional nickname associated with Mercedes-branded racing efforts.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team lineup alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as the energy drinks conglomerate's secondary racing division.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that debuted in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team structure, alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a sister team within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been a dominant force in Formula One since its establishment in 2005. Christian Horner led the team through its first two decades before departing in 2025, succeeded by Laurent Mekies as team principal. The squad represents one of two Formula One operations controlled by the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name.
